It started as nothing more than a silly hobby, really: Phainon enjoyed playing videogames as much as he did going to the gym in his free time. And as much as he too enjoyed his own solitude, sometimes it was almost unbearable to be idle in front of the bright computer screen, having nobody to share his unimportant yet spontaneous thoughts with. He was a restless man, after all, Cifera had said just before suggesting live streaming. Initially he just brushed it off, as his friend had said it with no intent other than jest, but really— would it be such a crazy thing to do?

And so, with little to ponder, he created an account on Genesis and set up all he needed on his desk to begin this new hobby of his: his customized home-built computer and a dusty old camera, courtesy of Castorice. Truthfully, it was nothing he did with much thought, or any expectations at all: but if he could talk at least one person's ear off and entertain them with it, then he'd be satisfied.

Surprising   no one but himself, though, his undeniable charisma and easygoing personality was enough to win over the community, and at a relatively fast pace at that. Plus, he was indeed very good at the games he showed: his playthroughs were as smooth and educational as possible. He has hardly processed his sudden and growing sucess in the platform, but one thing he's sure of is that he's grown to love the interaction it provides and the support of his followers.

Mydei stares down at his phone and snorts, turning it off and instead shifting his attention to his old laptop. Castorice's proposal came out of nowhere: they don't use to text much, after all, unless it's for a serious matter. So picture his surprise when he got a message for something as trivial as a play date she wanted to invite him to in someone else's behalf. Well, maybe play date isn't the right term: more like a showdown between two competitive players of the most unknown videogame ever created (her words, not his). Not that he could deny it: unless you ask an old man from an asylum, not many people will answer positively when asked if they know what Amphorean Chronicles is.

Doesn't mean it isn't the best  fighting game there is, at least in Mydei's eyes. He tried out its most primitive version in a rusty arcade, and fell in love with it right away. Unfortunately, he never really got the chance to enjoy its competitive and strategic factor— even the championships against veteran players felt all too easy.

So, naturally, when Castorice presented him the opportunity eleven year old Mydeimos would've sold all his stuff for —he was a disturbed kid, now that he thinks about it—, something urged him to go along. It could very well have been his inner child or his prideful ass refusing to deny competition.

He decides that the reason is of little relevance as he opens the Genesis site and browses for the account Castorice has so kindly provided, and his brows soon go up in surprise upon noting that his subscribers well surpass the million. It's a relatively small amount considering there's people on the site that average the ten million, but still. It hadn't crossed his mind that the guy might actually be a little famous.

It's odd, because Mydei does not recall having heard or seen of him— then again, he isn't the most knowledgeable man when it comes to stuff as such. He stops trying to search in his brain for any type of recollection once he opens his profile picture: Mydei hates that the first thing he thinks is that he is kind of handsome. Like, very handsome. So, objectively speaking, if he had seen a face like that before, he probably would still remember it.

He chooses not to dwell on the funny feeling of his belly and instead decides to scroll through his archived streams. He doesn't have to go too far to learn about Phainon's —that's the name Castorice has given to him— style: most of his streams consist of playthroughs of mostly action and fighting games, some horror games and a bit of simulators. As expected, probably. Mydei scrolls all the way back up and plugs in his headphones as he clicks on the most recent one: according to the page, it was recorded as of today.

The video takes a few seconds to load before Mydei is greeted by the same face that was smiling brightly on the account's profile, just that now his expression is a bit more casual, albeit still smiling. Must be his default resting face, he concludes, suddenly very much aware of his own scowl. The guy quickly accommodates the camera before finally greeting his viewers:

"Good evening, guys! Or morning. Or night. For me it's evening still," he says, letting out a soft giggle. Mydei sighs, in a non dreamy way. "I hope you're all set with your snacks and dogs, because today we're down for a long playthrough. As some of you might know, I'm going to be testing a new game with you. Ah, yes, and if you're new, welcome! And please do remember to check the rules." Mydei feels called out. He does not check the rules, instead moving his cursor down to the progress bar and skips near the end of the recording, precisely to the third hour.

Phainon seems to have quieted down, if the way his shoulders are slightly slumped are anything to go by, but he's still as talkative. He doesn't say anything Mydei understands, as it's probably about the game, but he still observes with some attention the behavior of his viewers: though there's plenty of messages going through the chatbox, they seem to be a relatively nice community. Not that he particularly cares, but he does feel a little bit more assured knowing that they'll probably not bite his head off.

He's already made up his mind. Not that there was much to think about, really: Castorice is incredibly perceptive despite what others might think, and if she deemed that extending him the invitation was a good enough idea, then he trusts her judgment. Plus, he was not about to turn down a challenge that was already laid on the table. No way.

"I can guarantee that you're all going to enjoy Amphorean Chronicles as much as I do! I can't believe so many of you guys don't know the game, but I'll make sure you get the full grasp of it. Nobody beats me when it comes to it, after all," he says, winking to the camera.

His viewers just leave appreciative comments saying how cute it is for him to be so passionate about the game and encouraging him as a pro, but Mydei's eye has the urge to twitch.

Ah. He can't let this slide now, can he?

He hurries to shut down his laptop, lest it overheats, and opens his chat with Castorice.

Phainon does a double check to make sure he's indeed at the right location. He also checks the time for good measure, although it's impossible for him to have messed that up. He sighs with relief when everything seems to be in order, and checks himself on his phone's camera if only out of instinct to know he looks at least presentable.

Mydei had said it was small and not really frequented, therefore making it a good place to talk. In any other situation Phainon would've had his doubts, but if Castorice trusted the guy, he trusted him too. Still, Phainon has been a bit of a nervous wreck since he awoke. Alas, he can't help it: he always gets a little anxious before meeting new people, afraid he won't make a good impression. Plus, this guy is a potential special guest on his channel, so he wants to make an extra good impression. That, and the fact that Castorice didn't said much at all besides the fact that he can be hot headed sometimes.

So, yeah.

He forces himself to ease his gut with one deep breath before he steps inside the shop, the bell on top of the door loudly announcing his presence. Behind the front desk is a man, probably in his thirties or so, and speaking to him is another. Phainon immediately guesses that must be Mydei, if the dawn-colored hair serves as a clue. That's the only pointer Castorice provided. He gives a little wave to the one he presumes is the shop owner, and just as he's about to speak, Mydei turns around.

But, truly, he's not exaggerating in the slightest— amber eyes with a feline touch, delicate yet sharp features and, God, are those tattoos adorning his very prominent muscles? He nods with  gratitude in his eyes, and the man gives him a tiny smile. "Welcome, then. I'm Kyros. I presume you're already acquaintanced with Mydeimos."

Mydei squints his eyes and then opens them just as fast, as if he had an idea. "Ah. The one with the wheat fields?"

Mydei wasn't lying when he said it wasn't too frequented. That's fine, though. The place has its charm.

"So, Mydei," he starts, fully turning around to properly face him. "Does this saturday work for you? Around four in the afternoon."

He thinks for a moment, ultimately deciding he has no plans at all. "Sure. Just send me the location and I'll be there."

Phainon gives him a thumbs up. "Great! You're not as hard to talk to as I thought."

Mydei frowns. "What's that supposed to mean?"

"You give off a totally intimidating vibe, that's all," he says, raising his hands as surrender as Mydei's frown deepens. "Anyway, better get going before it gets too late. Goodbye, Mydeimos! I'll send you the details once I get home. Be safe!"

He whips his head around, his eyes meeting with Mydei's. The latter smirks.

"I'm also looking forward to it."

Should his teacher see him now, he would with no doubt reprimend him for his childishness, but he's way past that.

He needs to wipe that infuriating, confident smirk off Phainon's face.

He just hopes not to come across bold. He's heard enough of Hephaestion's teasing for a lifetime.
